yesterday_lede: We hold the clock at 85.0 seconds, with the single biggest concern being the surge of extreme weather events across multiple regions.

chair.lede: We hold the clock at 84.1 seconds, with the biggest shift coming from a new human bird‑flu case and a coordinated fridge‑cyberattack in Europe.
body: The baseline remains unchanged for climate extremes, the Congo anthrax outbreak, and the earlier fake nuclear alerts, as no new developments altered those risks.
A Washington state resident died after contracting avian influenza, marking the first confirmed human case of this strain in the United States and adding a fresh biological pressure.
Across Europe, supermarkets experienced a coordinated cyberattack that seized refrigeration units, threatening food supply chains and representing a new AI‑tech infrastructure threat.

experts.say: No new nuclear weapon tests, treaty changes, or credible threats appeared; the North Korea drill comment and the fake warning are not new dangers.
Recent flash floods in the Southwest and a cyclone threat in India add more extreme weather events, but they fall under the already‑tracked climate‑extreme pressure, so no new change.

A Washington state resident died after contracting avian influenza, indicating a new human bird‑flu case and potential spread beyond animals (headlines 3, 8). This adds a fresh biological threat not covered by the existing anthrax pressure.
A coordinated cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe represents a new infrastructure threat not covered by existing pressures.
No new developments beyond the ongoing Ukraine conflict and other existing pressures.
